Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude slips as Iran-Oman talks fuel hopes of peace deal, Hormuz reopening
Article Text:
Oil prices edged lower as investors weighed whether progress in Iran-Oman talks could pave the way for a US-Iran peace deal

NEW DELHI: Oil prices edged lower on Thursday as investors weighed whether progress in Iran-Oman talks could pave the way for a US-Iran peace deal, potentially ending the five-month conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude futures fell 37 cents, or 0.5%, to $79.08 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined 53 cents, or 0.7%, to $74.69 a barrel.Earlier on Wednesday, Brent had settled slightly higher, while WTI ended marginally lower after recovering from two sessions of sharp losses.Market sentiment remains focused on diplomatic efforts to end the conflict after reports that Iran and Oman are working on a proposal aimed at resolving tensions between Tehran and Washington.According to Reuters, the proposed agreement would give Iran control over ships entering the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, marking one of the biggest concessions discussed so far.However, US officials have repeatedly maintained that Washington would never agree to Iran controlling access to the strategic waterway, despite President Donald Trump 's recent claim that a deal to reopen the strait was imminent.The Strait of Hormuz carries nearly a fifth of the world's oil supplies, making any disruption or reopening crucial for global energy markets.Meanwhile, geopolitical risks remain elevated. Iran has warned Gulf countries that any fresh US military strike on its territory would trigger retaliatory attacks on critical energy infrastructure across the region.Adding to supply concerns, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed on Wednesday that they had launched missile attacks on two Saudi oil tankers, one near the Red Sea port of Yanbu and another in the Gulf of Aden. However, Saudi Arabia has not confirmed either incident.On the supply front, fresh US inventory data also weighed on prices.The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) said crude oil inventories rose by 2.5 million barrels to 407 million barrels in the week ended July 31, compared with analysts' expectations of a 1.5 million-barrel decline. The increase came as refinery activity eased slightly and crude imports edged higher.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 37 cents, or 0.5%, to $79.08 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined 53 cents to $74.69 a barrel. Market sentiment remains focused on diplomatic efforts to end the conflict after reports that Iran and Oman are working on a proposal aimed at resolving tensions.

Article Title: Rupee hits 1-month closing high despite RBI repo rate pause; sliding crude oil prices help
Article Text:
Market participants said that any appreciation of the rupee beyond the 95-per-dollar mark is likely to trigger fresh demand for the US currency.

Lower oil prices help

The rupee strengthened to a one-month high on Wednesday, supported by lower crude oil prices. However, gains were trimmed after the Reserve Bank of India delivered its widely anticipated decision to keep policy rates unchanged.The currency opened 0.5% stronger at 94.92 against the US dollar, its highest level since July 1. It later gave up nearly half of its early advance to settle at 95.1175 per dollar, its strongest closing level since July 7.According to Dilip Parmar, Foreign Exchange Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, the RBI's decision to maintain the status quo on interest rates, along with a rebound in the US dollar and oil prices, weighed on the rupee after its initial rally."From a technical standpoint, the spot USD/INR is seeing immediate support around 94.75 and resistance near 95.60. Although the macro bias for the pair remains structurally weak, short-term bargain hunting could push the currency toward resistance levels," he told Reuters.Oil prices played a key role in driving currency movements. Benchmark Brent crude had fallen more than 12% over the previous two sessions on hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the five-month-long US-Iran conflict.However, prices recovered on Wednesday after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacked a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea.Also Read | As gold, stock markets lose lustre - why your humble fixed deposit is forever The sharp decline in crude prices earlier this week supported the rupee, which has appreciated 1.4% over the past eight trading sessions. Traders also attributed the positive sentiment to a recent pickup in foreign exchange inflows.Market participants said that any appreciation of the rupee beyond the 95-per-dollar mark is likely to trigger fresh demand for the US currency.The RBI left both its benchmark policy rate and policy stance unchanged on Wednesday as policymakers awaited clearer evidence on whether volatile crude oil prices would translate into broader inflationary pressures.Opinions on the policy outlook remain divided. Sonal Badhan, Economist at state-owned Bank of Baroda, expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points in December to prevent real interest rates from turning negative and to support the rupee.Meanwhile, dollar-rupee forward premiums declined during the session, broadly mirroring movements in the spot market. The one-year implied yield eased by 7 basis points to 2.79%.Also Read | US-Iran conflict, El Nino: Why RBI did not hike repo rate despite headwinds
Article Summary: The currency opened 0.5% stronger at 94.92 against the US dollar, its highest level since July 1. However, gains were trimmed after the Reserve Bank of India delivered its widely anticipated decision to keep policy rates unchanged. The sharp decline in crude prices earlier this week supported the rupee.

Article Title: Trump slams Exxon Mobil, Chevron for 'making too much money'; asks to give it back to consumers
Article Text:
What are US oil makers without Trump’s genius



Industry says prices reflect global market pressures



US oil giants are "making too much money", and Donald Trump is not happy about it.US President Donald Trump on Monday took aim at Exxon Mobil and Chevron, accusing the oil producers of profiting from supply shortages while motorists continue to pay elevated fuel prices. He further urged them to cut retail fuel prices instead of posting record earnings.The remarks came days after both companies reported strong quarterly results, helped by higher crude prices following supply disruptions in the Middle East and improved refining margins. The earnings have drawn renewed attention as the Trump administration faces growing pressure to show it is tackling high petrol prices ahead of the November midterm elections.Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said the companies were profiting too much from the current situation.“Based on a shortage, they’re making too much money,” Trump said. “I don’t like it, and I should be the last one to say because I’m a big free enterprise guy — nobody bigger.”He then singled out the country's two largest oil producers.“Chevron, too much money. Exxon Mobil, too much, too much money,” Trump said.“They ought to give some of that back to the public, and they better cut the retail price, the consumer price.”The average retail price of gasoline in the United States has stayed around $4.10 a gallon over the past week, compared with less than $3 before the United States and Israel launched attacks against Iran in February.Trump's criticism was not limited to the companies' profits. Earlier in the day, he also took aim at Chevron Chairman and chief executive Mike Wirth after the executive discussed the company's performance during an interview with Fox Business.Posting on Truth Social, Trump said Wirth had failed to acknowledge what he described as his administration's role in the industry's current success.“Mike Wirth, chairman and CEO of Chevron, just gave, in an interview with the fabulous Maria Bartiromo, all of the reasons that his company is doing so well. The only thing he conveniently forgot to mention is that, without the genius, foresight, strength, and stability of the Trump Administration, the Oil Industry, and our Country itself, would be dead!”Trump also referred to Chevron's business in Venezuela, saying the company was now benefiting after previously being forced out.“They threw Mike and Chevron out of Venezuela, but now they're back, far bigger and stronger than ever before, expecting to make a fortune!”He concluded the post by demanding that oil producers immediately lower prices charged to consumers.“That goes for other Oil Companies as well...and get your consumer (retail!) Oil Prices down, now!”Trump's latest comments follow an order he issued in late June directing the Justice Department to investigate whether major oil companies had failed to lower fuel prices quickly enough after crude oil prices eased. Even so, retail gasoline prices are generally set by the independent retailers who own petrol stations rather than by oil producers.During earnings calls on Friday, executives from both companies cautioned that limited refining capacity could keep petrol prices elevated through the autumn.The American Petroleum Institute also rejected suggestions that individual companies were responsible for higher prices.Andrea Woods, a spokesperson for the industry body, said fuel prices were being shaped by international market conditions.“Driven by global supply, demand and continued uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz and other critical shipping lanes—not by any one company.”“Our industry shares the goal of delivering affordable, reliable energy for consumers,” she added, as cited by Politico.Meanwhile, global oil markets remained volatile as tensions in the Middle East continued to keep traders on edge. Oil prices edged higher on Tuesday after tumbling in the previous session, with concerns over potential supply disruptions resurfacing amid fading hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran war. Front-month Brent crude futures rose 62 cents, or 0.7%, to $84.39 a barrel by 0055 GMT, recovering some losses after slumping 7% on Monday to their lowest level in three weeks.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump takes aim at Exxon Mobil and Chevron. Accuses oil producers of profiting from supply shortages. Urges them to cut retail fuel prices instead of posting record earnings. Comments come days after both companies reported strong quarterly results.

Article Title: New stock market timings from August 3: What has changed?
Article Text: Final minutes of the trading day are set to change from Monday, August 3, as the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is introducing a new Closing Auction Session for F&O-eligible stocks and extending trading hours for the equity derivatives segment.The new framework brings a different end-of-day routine for traders, especially those in F&O-eligible stocks and the equity derivatives segment. Here's a look at what will change starting this week.Under the revised trading framework, biggest change will be seen in the closing process for F&O-eligible (Category I) stocks. Instead of ending with the regular trading session alone, these stocks will now move into a dedicated auction process after 3:15pm, with the auction-discovered price becoming their official closing price.Regular trading for F&O-eligible stocks will end at 3:15pm, followed by a five-minute transition period until 3:20pm. The Closing Auction Session will then begin with CAS Order Entry I from 3:20pm to 3:25pm and CAS Order Entry II from 3:25pm to 3:30pm.During the second order entry window, market orders cannot be modified or cancelled. At the same time, the session will also close randomly within its final two minutes.Order matching will be carried out between 3:30pm and 3:35pm, after which the closing auction price will be determined. This price will be treated as the official closing price for all F&O-eligible stocks.The changes do not affect all stocks. Non-F&O equity cash stocks will continue to trade until 3:30pm, with no change in their existing market hours.Sebi has also extended trading in the equity derivatives (F&O) segment by 10 minutes. From August 3, trading in this segment will continue until 3:40pm, while operating hours for other market segments will remain unchanged.The regulator has also revised the pre-opening session.Under the new schedule, order entry will take place from 9:00 am to 9:07 am, followed by order matching between 9:07am and 9:15am. The regular trading session will continue to start at 9:15 am.According to Sebi, the Closing Auction Session is intended to ensure a fair and transparent closing price through an auction mechanism. It said the framework is designed to improve execution efficiency by aggregating liquidity, provide equal access to all investors, reduce tracking errors for passive funds, and align India's market structure with global best practices.
Article Summary: Sebi is introducing a new Closing Auction Session for F&O-eligible stocks and extending trading hours for the equity derivatives segment. The changes do not affect all stocks. Non-F&O equity cash stocks will continue to trade until 3:30pm, with no change in their existing market hours.

Article Title: Google rejigs AI leadership as DeepMind CEO shifts role
Article Text:
The shake-up comes during a pivotal juncture for Google DeepMind: the flagship version of its latest Gemini model remains unreleased

Google parent company Alphabet on Wednesday announced a leadership overhaul of its AI division, with AI chief Demis Hassabis leaving his main managerial role and as several leaders of its Gemini model, including veteran engineer Jeff Dean, left the company to launch a startup called Discovery Loop. The shake-up comes during a pivotal juncture for Google DeepMind: the flagship version of its latest Gemini model remains unreleased despite a planned June launch, sparking investor and industry concerns that Google is falling behind its rivals Anthropic and OpenAI, each of which scooped up a star Google AI staffer this summer.Shares of Alphabet fell 4% after the news. Hassabis, a Nobel Prize recipient, will take the newly created title of Alphabet’s chief scientist and transition from being Google DeepMind CEO to being its chairman, he said in a memo to staff.Koray Kavukcuoglu, the unit’s chief technology officer, will assume day-to-day responsibilities of DeepMind in addition to his parallel role as Alphabet’s chief AI architect.
Article Summary: Google parent company Alphabet on Wednesday announced a leadership overhaul of its AI division, with AI chief Demis Hassabis leaving his main managerial role. Hassabis, a Nobel Prize recipient, will take the newly created title of Alphabet’s chief scientist and transition from being Google DeepMind CEO to being its chairman.

Article Title: ‘Zero tolerance for unethical practices at HDFC’
Article Text:
Kumar described governance risks as isolated and manageable events rather than structural failures

MUMBAI: HDFC Bank ’s newly appointed chairman Rajiv Kumar said the lender’s corporate governance remains fundamentally uncompromised, while asserting that the board will ensure control functions stay fully empowered with zero tolerance for unethical practices.Addressing leadership changes and external scrutiny after the exit of the previous chairman, Kumar rejected claims of systemic governance lapses and said oversight, transparency, and execution remain intact. His predecessor and former economic affairs secretary Atanu Chakraborty had quit earlier this year citing `values and ethics’. Kumar, who was earlier the finance secretary and chief election commissioner, said that “the bank’s ethos and internal control systems are strong. I assure you that this will be further strengthened and empowered”.He said that after the resignation, the bank appointed external legal counsel under the supervision of independent directors to examine the allegations, with findings disclosed to stock exchanges on June 26, 2026. “Let me reiterate, on my behalf and on behalf of the Board, that the bank is fundamentally strong, with a pristine balance sheet. There are no governance related concerns at the systemic level,” he said.Kumar described governance risks as isolated and manageable events rather than structural failures, and said existing processes are designed to detect and address such issues. “Strong institutions are defined by how good the policy and processes are, across their operating and governance domains.“The process should identify issues, investigate them, act upon them, disclose them where required and hold everyone involved accountable. This process is what allows institutions to become trustworthy as it ensures that any potential cause for concern that arises can be addressed on a case to basis and systemic improvements introduced in a wholesome manner to plug gaps to prevent recurrence,” he said.He added that the bank has demonstrated the presence of control systems and oversight at committee levels to identify deviations, if any. “The Board will ensure that control functions remain fully empowered to have zero tolerance towards any unethical practice, which will be dealt with speed and firmness on a case-to-case basis,” he said.On operations, Kumar said the bank faces balance sheet adjustments after its merger with HDFC, which have affected net interest margin and CASA ratio. He said the lender aims to improve these metrics over the next two to three years by increasing deposit market share and expanding consumption-led lending.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank ’s newly appointed chairman Rajiv Kumar said the lender’s corporate governance remains uncompromised. Kumar rejected claims of systemic governance lapses and said oversight, transparency, and execution remain intact. His predecessor and former economic affairs secretary Atanu Chakraborty had quit earlier this year citing `values and ethics’

Article Title: Airtel Money eyes London listing this year, telco gets ARPU boost
Article Text:
Airtel Money has now achieved meaningful scale with Q1 revenue of over $400 million, growing at 26% year-on-year in constant currency terms

NEW DELHI: Airtel Money is preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026, Bharti Airtel executive VC Gopal Vittal said on Wednesday. Airtel Money is a mobile commerce service that allows money transfer via the phone.“Airtel Money has now achieved meaningful scale with Q1 revenue of over $400 million, growing at 26% year-on-year in constant currency terms. The opportunity ahead remains significant, with 64% of adults across our footprint still without access to a formal bank account.“Given this growth trajectory and the large addressable opportunity, Airtel Money is now preparing for a London listing in the second half of 2026,” he said.The move comes at a time when Bharti Airtel reported 37% profit growth in the first quarter thanks largely to consumers opting for higher value packages, increased data usage, strong customer additions and growth across its India and Africa businesses, while tariffs remained the same. As a result, Airtel’s average revenue per user (ARPU) increased to Rs 264 during the quarter from Rs 250 a year ago.“Our focus remains on accelerating ARPU growth through portfolio premiumisation on mobile, while continuing to maintain a competitive share of customer net additions.Post-paid is a key output growth lever for us with significant opportunity ahead of us... Within pre-paid itself, we continue to see a large opportunity to move customers to their most relevant plans by using customer context and next best action capabilities on our digital stack. In addition, handset upgrades from feature phones to smartphones, rising data usage, 5G adoption and international roaming provide meaningful headroom for ARPU expansion going forward,” Vital said during an investor call, adding that the Africa business is also reporting strong growth.Airtel India MD and CEO Shashwat Sharma said: “(In Q1) we added 33 lakh revenue-earning customers and 50 lakh smartphone data customers. We added 10 lakh postpaid customers this quarter, which is the highest-level addition in any quarter for us. Postpaid customers now account for 8% plus of our total customer base.” The company completed a share swap transaction in Q1 that increased its stake in Airtel Africa to more than 79%.
Article Summary: Airtel Money is a mobile commerce service that allows money transfer via the phone. Bharti Airtel reported 37% profit growth in the first quarter thanks largely to consumers opting for higher value packages, increased data usage, strong customer additions.

Article Title: Rupees 10 and 20 polymer notes to be in circulation by early FY28
Article Text:
Central bank is preparing to pilot the new currency substrate after securing govt approval for large-scale field trials

MUMBAI: Polymer banknotes are likely to enter circulation at the beginning of FY28, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said, as the central bank prepares to pilot the new currency substrate after securing govt approval for large-scale field trials. The Centre has permitted the RBI to print two billion pieces of polymer notes initially for field trials, the government informed Parliament on Monday. RBI has floated a tender to source material.

Article Title: Repo rate unchanged, RBI sees higher growth, lower inflation
Article Text:
RBI noted that core inflation excluding precious metals stood at 2.3% to 2.5%, while headline inflation pressures were driven largely by supply-side factors

MUMBAI: RBI raised its growth projections and lowered inflation estimates while the monetary policy committee voted unanimously to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% and retain a neutral stance, signalling no immediate rate hike this year despite concerns among forecasters.“There is a need for greater clarity to emerge, especially regarding inflation, its path and composition before taking any policy action,” RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said, even as the MPC revised the core inflation forecast for FY27 downward by 40 basis points to 4.3% from 4.7% made in June 2027.The central bank reiterated the same set of risks, citing the resumption of West Asia conflict, deficient or uneven monsoon conditions amid El Niño, and sharp two-way movements in global oil prices. According to Soumya Kanti Ghosh, chief economist, SBI group, the policy communicates less uncertainty and is more dovish compared to the June statement.“Clearly, the RBI policy statement pushes out any rate hikes in FY27 with inflation also remaining benign at 5% and core inflation at 4.3%,” said Ghosh.RBI said underlying demand pressures remain benign. It noted that core inflation excluding precious metals stood at 2.3% to 2.5%, while headline inflation pressures were driven largely by supply-side factors such as food and fuel rather than broad-based demand. Overall CPI inflation was reduced by 10 basis points to 5.0%, after Q1 inflation came in 30 basis points lower than earlier estimates due to limited pass-through of cost pressures.The governor said that real GDP growth for 2026-27 is projected at 6.7%, with Q1 at 7.0%, Q2 at 6.4%, Q3 at 6.5%, and Q4 at 6.8%.
Article Summary: RBI raised its growth projections and lowered inflation estimates while the monetary policy committee voted unanimously to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%. The central bank reiterated the same set of risks, citing the resumption of West Asia conflict, deficient or uneven monsoon conditions amid El Niño.

Article Title: Tata Sons continues to be in upper layer, RBI indicates
Article Text:
The classification has gained attention after Tata Sons sought to de-register as an NBFC to avoid mandatory listing requirements

MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated that Tata Sons continues to be on the list of upper layer NBFCs, even as the central bank is yet to release its updated classification based on revised principle-based criteria. Malhotra said the identification of upper layer NBFCs is now principle-based and entities that meet the criteria are automatically included, with size remaining the key determinant. “It is now principle-based, so as per those principles, everyone knows what the list is and can understand it. I think the list will be out very soon — we have changed the rules, so [we will] reissue the list,” he said.The classification has gained attention after Tata Sons sought to de-register as an NBFC to avoid mandatory listing requirements, while the Shapoorji Pallonji group, the largest shareholder, has pushed for a listing. The RBI has not yet made its periodic disclosure of NBFCs in the upper layer. One of the norms for upper layer NBFCs is compulsory listing. Tata Sons had earlier repaid all its debts to avoid mandatory listing and stay private.Malhotra said entities above a defined threshold are automatically classified into the upper layer, and market participants are aware of NBFCs falling into each category. An entity that has applied for surrender of its registration certification will remain on the list until a revised list is issued.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated that Tata Sons continues to be on the list of upper layer NBFCs. The central bank is yet to release its updated classification based on revised principle-based criteria. The classification has gained attention after Tata Sons sought to de-register as an NBFC.

Article Title: RBI proposes uniform interest rate norms for banks, NBFCs
Article Text:
The new norms will impact all non-bank lenders, including housing finance companies and microfinance providers

MUMBAI: RBI’s move to harmonise interest rate frameworks across regulated entities is likely to standardise loan pricing and improve monetary transmission while reducing the pricing discretion currently available to NBFCs.The move would mark a departure from the existing structure where commercial banks operate under structured benchmark systems, while NBFCs retain greater flexibility through internal, board-approved prime lending rate models. According to the broad direction of policy, the central bank is likely to extend principle-based interest rate rules across lenders to curb arbitrary pricing and strengthen consumer protection.The new norms will impact all non-bank lenders, including housing finance companies and microfinance providers. The framework is expected to push NBFCs towards standardised benchmarking of floating rate loans. Under current bank rules, retail and MSME floating rate loans are linked to an external benchmark rate such as the RBI repo rate or treasury bill yields, while other floating loans are tied to internal benchmarks such as MCLR.NBFCs could be required to adopt recognised external benchmarks for retail and MSME loans or formal internal benchmarks instead of internal prime rates. They may also be required to follow a uniform benchmark within each loan category to improve predictability for borrowers.RBI is also likely to introduce standardised reset timelines for floating rate loans. At present, NBFC practices allow flexibility in resetting rates, which can result in slower transmission of rate cuts compared to hikes. Under the expected alignment, external benchmark-linked loans may require resets at least once every three months, while internal benchmark-linked loans could have a maximum reset period of one year.Loan agreements are likely to be required to clearly specify reset dates to improve transparency.
Article Summary: RBI’s move to harmonise interest rate frameworks across regulated entities is likely to standardise loan pricing. The new norms will impact all non-bank lenders, including housing finance companies and microfinance providers. The framework is expected to push NBFCs towards standardised benchmarking of floating rate loans.

Article Title: No rollback of closing auction session: Sebi
Article Text:
Sebi insists on creating better awareness among investing community in a meeting with brokers

Insists On Creating Better Awareness Among Investing Community In A Meet With Brokers

MUMBAI: Faced with teething troubles with the Closing Auction Session (CAS), officials at markets regulator Sebi on Wednesday interacted with representatives from large broking houses to understand the problems and asked them to make investors aware of the system. CAS is the newly introduced system for closing price discovery for stocks that are also traded in the derivatives segment of the bourses.During the meeting, the regulator also asked brokers to display the prices discovered through CAS on their apps and trading platforms, figures that many investors have been saying were missing from some of those platforms. According to people in the know, Sebi told brokers that the system would not be rolled back. The meeting with brokers came a day after stock exchanges took feedback from market participants to understand the initial glitches that traders and investors were facing in CAS.One of the major pain points for market participants was the sharp spike in the value of Nifty 50 index on NSE , between the time when normal trading closed at 3.15pm and the post-CAS closing at 3.30pm. Sensex on the BSE , however, didn’t show much spike in values. Traders also pointed out that there was divergence between the prices of the same stock on NSE and BSE. According to a trader, the sudden spike in prices and index values on NSE was because more institutional traders trade on NSE than on BSE.
Article Summary: Sebi insists on creating better awareness among investing community in a meeting with brokers. CAS is the newly introduced system for closing price discovery for stocks that are also traded in the derivatives segment of the bourses. According to people in the know, Sebi told brokers that the system would not be rolled back.

Article Title: Consumers already bearing UPI costs indirectly: RBI governor Malhotra
Article Text:
In the past, RBI officials have supported fees at least for large transactions

MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said consumers already bear the cost of UPI transactions through the broader economy even if merchant fees are not explicitly charged.Responding to questions at a press conference on enabling merchant fees on UPI, Malhotra said it was too early to take a view, and the focus remains on strengthening the payments infrastructure. “It is very premature right now. Now, costs have to be paid by someone — it’s a public [good]; we all want this particular infrastructure to continue to strengthen, become more efficient. That’s our focus as of now — let’s watch how developments proceed,” he said.In the past, RBI officials have supported fees at least for large transactions. Govt has proposed amendments to the law that barred any form of merchant fees on UPI transactions. There have also been reports that the government plans to allow merchant fees to be charged on UPI transactions with a value of over Rs 2,000. The absence of fees has resulted in banks ceding the payments as a service space to fintechs, with the likes of PhonePe and Google Pay being an almost duopoly, using the transactions to draw more users to their platform, where they seek to earn revenue through distribution of many other services.Malhotra said the objective is to scale up UPI usage significantly and any decision on fees must consider its impact on adoption. “The goal is to have 800 million transactions a day or so. So, imposing a fee... let’s wait, it’s premature right now. But please keep in mind that ultimately it is the consumer, in some way or the other, who is already paying it — it may not be the same consumer; it may be the general economy, and you don’t get to see it directly, but it’s already happening in some form,” he said. He said the priority is to ensure sustained investment in UPI and the availability of revenue streams to support its growth.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said consumers already bear the cost of UPI transactions through the broader economy. In the past, RBI officials have supported fees at least for large transactions. Govt has proposed amendments to the law that barred any form of merchant fees on UPI.

Article Title: Government mops up 31.5k cr from LIC share sale
Article Text:
Dipam secretary said that after offloading 6.5% in LIC, public shareholding in the life insurance major is now at 10% level,

MUMBAI: The government has mobilised Rs 31,552 crore by divesting a 6.5% stake in life insurance major LIC through the offer for sale (OFS) that closed on Wednesday. Compared to 82.2 crore shares that were on offer, including the greenshoe option, total demand stood at 111.3 crore shares. Given the strong response, the shares were allotted at Rs 383.69 per share, slightly higher than the base price of Rs 382 per share.The Rs 31,552-crore fund raise made the LIC OFS the biggest public offer in the Indian stock market.Dipam secretary Arunish Chawla said on X that after offloading 6.5% in LIC, public shareholding in the life insurance major is now at the 10% level, and “it has achieved this critical milestone ahead of schedule.” The top govt official was indicating meeting Sebi’s minimum public shareholding norm for listed companies.
Article Summary: The Rs 31,552-crore fund raise made the LIC OFS the biggest public offer in the Indian stock market. Dipam secretary Arunish Chawla said that after offloading 6.5% in LIC, public shareholding in the life insurance major is now at the 10% level.

Article Title: Ex-Ethiopian Air chief Tewolde Gebremariam becomes Air India CEO
Article Text:
Gebremariam had spent over 36 years in Africa’s largest airline, where he served in various roles

Pakistan International Airlines also wanted Gebremariam as head

NEW DELHI: Air India on Wednesday announced former Ethiopian Airlines group CEO Tewolde Gebremariam as its next CEO and MD, succeeding Campbell Wilson.Gebremariam had spent over 36 years in Africa’s largest airline, where he served in various roles, including as regional director for India and South Asia in 1995-96, before quitting the group in March 2022 to become a senior strategic adviser to US carrier Delta. Incidentally, Pakistan International Airlines had also selected Gebremariam as CEO.Pakistan International Airlines, which was privatised last December and the new majority stakeholder is trying to revive it, had also selected Gebremariam, given his contribution in making Ethiopian emerge as Africa’s largest airline.The Tata Group, which is trying to revive Air India and Air India Express after acquiring it in Jan 2022, has managed to steal the march on PIA in getting the former Ethiopian boss.Subject to getting all required approvals, which should not be an issue as Ethiopia is a friendly country unlike a Turkish national Tatas had chosen soon after taking over Air India, and who did not get security clearance, Gebremariam could join next month, taking over from current incumbent Campbell Wilson.While Air India’s attempted turnaround is the most difficult one in contemporary aviation due to challenges like legacy issues compounded by post-Covid supply chain constraints and airspace constraints, the AI 171 crash last June has made matters worse for the Maharaja.The airline lost almost Rs 23,000 crore last fiscal, and this year is also proving to be a tough one for all airlines globally.In such a situation, Air India says its board had to “identify a leader with a proven record of managing mega-scale airline turnarounds, delivering operational excellence, fostering a strong culture of safety and service, and driving profitable expansion…. Gebremariam possesses the ideal combination of leadership, deep operational expertise and strategic execution capability required for Air India’s next phase of growth. ”N Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons and Air India, said: “Having completed the initial phase of stabilisation, integration, and fleet commitments under Campbell’s guidance, Air India is now entering a critical execution and expansion era. Tewolde’s track record in building one of the world’s most efficient and profitable airline groups makes him uniquely suited to lead Air India.”Tewolde Gebremariam said, “Air India carries an incredible legacy, and the opportunity to build a world-class global airline that reflects India’s extraordinary economic potential is uniquely exciting. I look forward to working closely with chairman Chandrasekaran, the board, our employees, and all government and industry partners to deliver exceptional operational reliability, warm Indian hospitality, and sustained long-term growth. ”
Article Summary: Air India on Wednesday announced former Ethiopian Airlines group CEO Tewolde Gebremariam as its next CEO and MD. He will take over from current incumbent Campbell Wilson. Pakistan International Airlines, which was privatised last December and the new majority stakeholder is trying to revive it, had also selected Geb Remariam.

Article Title: Liquidity surge due to NRI deposits to be limited and temporary: RBI
Article Text:
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra addresses a press conference on Monetary Policy Statement and Post-Monetary Policy, in Mumbai, Maharashtra. (@reservebankofindia593/Yt via PTI Photo)(PTI08_05_2026_000027B)

MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said inflows from the special FCNR(B) deposit scheme for non-residents will have a temporary and limited impact on liquidity, with surplus conditions expected to ease after peaking around the second quarter.Malhotra said the central bank did not have any target for dollar mobilisation under the scheme, which has seen inflows of over $36 billion in the last three weeks in July , and there was no proposal to either advance its closure or extend it. He said liquidity conditions will remain in surplus only briefly. “liquidity may be in surplus only for the very short term. It may peak around Q2, around September or so, and going forward it should absorb, because of our normal needs of the economy - - through increasing currency in circulation, higher requirement for reserves because of deposit growth. We also have some forwards which are getting matured,” he said.He said the liquidity impact is consistent with the annual infusion undertaken by RBI through open market operations and swap transactions. On the deployment of the dollars exchanged with banks, Malhotra said that it would be decided in the same way as other additions to forex reserves “there is a high-level committee, with members from the government also participating regularly, and we take a call on how to manage the reserves based on three principles of security, liquidity, and returns. But as I mentioned, the liquidity it will inject is there only for a short while — the balance sheet is growing at more or less a normal pace, barring a flood of unexpected deposits," said Malhotra.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said inflows from the special FCNR(B) deposit scheme for non-residents will have a temporary and limited impact on liquidity. He said the central bank did not have any target for dollar mobilisation under the scheme.

Article Title: RRB ALP CBT 2 answer key released at rrbapply.gov.in; objection window open until August 11, 2026
Article Text:
RRB ALP CBT 2 answer key 2026 released; response sheets available, objection window opens for candidates

RRB ALP CBT 2

answer key 2026:

Objection window and score calculation



Steps to download the answer key



Upcoming recruitment schedule



Vacancy details and selection process



The Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) has released the provisional answer key, question papers and recorded responses for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) CBT 2 examination conducted under CEN 01/2025. Candidates who appeared for the examination held on July 28, 2026, can now access the documents by logging in through the official RRB candidate login or DigiALM portal.Candidates are required to enter their registration number along with their date of birth or password to access the response sheet. The release of the provisional key enables candidates to compare their responses, estimate their scores and submit objections, if required, within the stipulated period. The CBT 1 answer key for the same recruitment cycle had earlier been released on March 20, 2026.The objection window will remain open from August 5 to August 11, 2026. Candidates can challenge any answer in the provisional key by paying an objection fee of Rs 50 per question. The fee will be refunded if the objection is accepted as valid after scrutiny.Candidates can estimate their scores using the prescribed marking scheme by awarding one mark for every correct response and deducting one-third mark for every incorrect answer.The final score will depend on the revised answer key issued after the objection review process.To access the response sheet, candidates should visit the regional RRB website or the DigiALM portal and click on the link for CEN 01/2025 – Assistant Loco Pilot CBT 2 Answer Key. After entering the required login credentials and completing the security verification, candidates can download their question paper, recorded responses and provisional answer key for future reference.According to the recruitment timeline, the last date to submit objections is August 11, 2026. The final answer key, CBT 2 scorecards and cut-offs are expected in September 2026. The Computer-Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) schedule is likely to be announced during September or October 2026.Meanwhile, the RRB ALP 2026 recruitment cycle under CEN 01/2026 has already concluded its application process. Registrations closed on June 14, 2026, while the application correction window remained open from June 17 to June 26, 2026. CBT 1 examination dates, city intimation slips and admit cards for the new recruitment cycle are expected to be released during August 2026.The current CEN 01/2025 recruitment is being conducted for 10,970 revised vacancies, while CEN 01/2026 has been notified for 11,127 vacancies. Both recruitment cycles offer Level 2 posts under the Seventh Central Pay Commission with an initial pay of Rs 19,900.The minimum qualifying percentage remains 40 per cent for UR and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) and SC candidates, and 25 per cent for ST candidates. For final merit preparation, CBT 2 Part A carries 70 per cent weightage, while the CBAT contributes the remaining 30 per cent. CBT 2 Part B is qualifying in nature and is not included in the final merit calculation.
Article Summary: The Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) has released the provisional answer key, question papers and recorded responses for the Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP) CBT 2 examination conducted under CEN 01/2025. Candidates who appeared for the examination held on July 28, 2026, can now access the documents by logging in through the official RRB candidate login or DigiALM portal. The release of the provisional key enables candidates to compare their responses and estimate their scores.

Article Title: US tightens immigration rules: Incomplete visa, green card applications can now be rejected outright
Article Text:
US tightens immigration rules, allows USCIS to deny incomplete visa and green card applications. (Representative image - AP photo)

Deny applications that fail to establish eligibility at the time of filing.

Reject requests submitted without the required initial supporting evidence.

Issue an RFE where they determine additional documentation is appropriate.

The United States has tightened its immigration benefit processing rules, allowing immigration officers to reject incomplete or insufficiently documented applications for visas, green cards, citizenship and other immigration benefits without first asking applicants to submit additional evidence. The change, which took effect immediately, could affect thousands of Indian applicants seeking to study, work or settle in the US.The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced that applicants must establish their eligibility for an immigration benefit at the time of filing. Under the revised guidance, if an application does not include all required initial evidence or fails to demonstrate eligibility, officers may deny the request without issuing a Request for Evidence (RFE) or a Notice of Intent to Deny (NOID)."The burden is on the requestor to establish that he or she is eligible for the requested benefit at the time of filing the benefit request and that he or she continues to be eligible through adjudication,” USCIS said.The agency said its application forms and accompanying instructions already specify the documents and evidence required for every immigration benefit, enabling applicants to submit complete requests at the time of filing.USCIS said the policy better aligns its procedures with the long-standing regulatory authority of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), strengthens the integrity of the immigration system and makes it more difficult for applicants to file what it described as frivolous benefit requests.The revised guidance marks a reversal of a policy adopted during the Biden administration, under which immigration officers were generally encouraged to issue Requests for Evidence before denying benefit applications, even when filings were incomplete or lacked documents required at the time of submission.According to USCIS, the earlier approach allowed incomplete or substantially deficient applications to slow the processing of other pending cases. The agency also said it enabled some applicants to file "placeholder" applications to obtain associated immigration benefits, such as employment authorisation, while waiting for a decision on their primary request.USCIS has now restored officers' discretion to deny benefit requests without first issuing an RFE or NOID in appropriate cases. However, officers will continue to retain the discretion to issue an RFE if they determine additional evidence is warranted before making a decision.Under the updated policy, immigration officers may:The agency said the changes would help allocate resources more efficiently, speed up case processing and reduce meritless applications that add to existing backlogs.The policy took effect immediately and applies to all immigration benefit requests pending or filed on or after August 5, 2026, unless existing regulations or USCIS policy provide otherwise.The move represents one of the latest changes to US immigration procedures aimed at tightening benefit adjudication standards. Applicants seeking employment-based visas, family-sponsored green cards, extensions or changes of status, naturalisation and other immigration benefits will now face greater pressure to ensure their applications are complete and fully documented at the time of filing, as incomplete submissions may no longer receive an opportunity for correction before being denied.
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced that applicants must establish their eligibility for an immigration benefit at the time of filing. The change, which took effect immediately, could affect thousands of Indian applicants seeking to study, work or settle in the US.

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street scales new record highs; oil prices hold steady
Article Text:
Markets have continued to rally as companies near the end of the latest earnings season.

US stock market today: Wall Street stocks moved higher in early trading on Wednesday, extending the record-setting momentum from the previous session, while oil prices remained largely stable.The S&P 500 advanced 0.5%. By 9:53 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had gained 487 points, or 0.9%, while the Nasdaq Composite was up 0.3%.Both the S&P 500 and the Dow closed at record highs on Tuesday, while the Nasdaq remained within 2% of its all-time peak. The major US indices have posted strong gains so far this week, giving August a solid start, according to an AP report.Markets have continued to rally as companies near the end of the latest earnings season with robust financial performance. About three-fourths of the companies in the S&P 500 have already reported quarterly results, and Wall Street expects overall profit growth of around 50% once the reporting season concludes.The Walt Disney Company was among the latest firms to report earnings, with its shares rising 3.2% after comfortably surpassing analysts' profit estimates. The strong performance was supported by $1 billion in box office collections from "Toy Story 5" and healthy revenue from its theme park businessBooking Holdings also posted strong gains, climbing 5.5% after reporting higher quarterly profit and revenue, driven by continued strength in travel demand.SpaceX shares fell 10.7%, even after the company reported a smaller quarterly loss than analysts had expected in its first earnings release since becoming a publicly listed company late Tuesday. However, the stock of semiconductor leader Nvidia climbed 3.9% after SpaceX announced that it would exclusively use Nvidia's chips to power its artificial intelligence systems.Robust corporate earnings and optimism about future profit growth have continued to support the stock market despite lingering concerns over elevated inflation.Investors also remained focused on developments in the US-Iran conflict, which continues to cloud market sentiment. President Donald Trump said an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached as early as Wednesday. However, the five-month-old conflict has seen repeated setbacks and renewed tensions, disrupting global oil supplies and creating volatility in energy markets.Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, edged up 0.1% to $79.41 per barrel.The bond market was relatively stable, with the yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note inching up to 4.64% from 4.63% at Tuesday's close.Asian equity markets ended higher, led by gains of more than 3% in Tokyo and Seoul as semiconductor and other AI-related stocks advanced. European markets also traded in positive territory.
Article Summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 487 points, or 0.9%, while the Nasdaq Composite was up 0.3%. Both the S&P 500 and the Dow closed at record highs on Tuesday. The major US indices have posted strong gains so far this week, giving August a solid start.

Article Title: SpaceX's first earnings: Revenue soars to $7.8 billion in debut results
Article Text:
SpaceX reports first quarterly earnings, posts $7.8 billion in revenue

Starlink keeps the business connected

Market cheers, then hesitates

All eyes on Starship

SpaceX delivered a quarter that beat expectations on paper, but not enough to put investors completely at ease.The Elon Musk-led company reported a smaller-than-expected loss for the three months through June as revenue soared to $7.8 billion, powered by rapid growth in its Starlink satellite internet business.At the same time, the company dramatically stepped up spending on artificial intelligence, infrastructure and research, a strategy Musk argued would speed up its path to becoming a trillion-dollar-a-year revenue company.SpaceX reported a loss of $541 million, or 9 cents per share, less than half of what Wall Street analysts had forecast. Revenue surged more than 90% from a year earlier.The Elon Musk-led company said it was on track to achieve a $100 billion annual revenue run rate by December. It also projected that investments in AI computing would pay for themselves in under a year, plans to deploy at least 1,000 next-generation V3 Starlink satellites over the next 12 months, and outlined ambitions to expand into services that compete with mobile phone providers.The biggest boost came from SpaceX's connectivity business, where revenue climbed 66% compared with the same period last year. The growth was fuelled by Starlink, whose subscriber base doubled to 12 million.“It's not out of the question that at some point, Starlink will deliver a majority of the world’s internet," Musk said in call with analysts.While revenue accelerated, so did spending.Infrastructure and research and development expenditure jumped to $18 billion, up from less than $3 billion a year ago. Chief financial officer Bret Johnsen said investors should expect capital expenditure to remain at similar levels over the next two quarters.Musk defended the aggressive investment, saying the additional spending would help SpaceX hit annual revenue of $1 trillion a year sooner than previously expected.According to Musk, the company is now on track to reach that milestone in 2030 instead of 2031.SpaceX shares climbed 9% during Tuesday's regular trading session before surrendering most of those gains in after-hours trade.The stock has lost roughly half its value since peaking in June, shortly after the company's initial public offering, which briefly made Musk the world's first trillionaire.Investors remain concerned that Musk may have oversold the company's prospects for both future space travel and its AI chatbot, Grok. Another source of uncertainty is the upcoming expiry of the lock-up provision, which will allow insiders to begin selling shares.From Thursday, more than 900 million shares will be released for trading, more than doubling the stock currently available in the market. It is the first of several tranches that will become eligible for trading over the coming months.The decline in SpaceX shares, along with losses in Tesla stock, has reduced Musk's wealth to $783 billion, according to Forbes.The earnings call also turned the spotlight on Starship, the massive rocket that sits at the centre of SpaceX's long-term ambitions.The spacecraft successfully deployed satellites during a test flight late last month. Musk said the next major test is expected at the end of this month, when the company will attempt to demonstrate Starship's reusability by catching both the spacecraft and its booster with mechanical arms as they return to base.NASA hopes to use Starship to send astronauts back to the Moon in the near future.“We want to put boots on the ground — boots on the moon — in 2028,” said SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell.SpaceX also operates the social media platform X, formerly Twitter.
Article Summary: SpaceX reported a loss of $541 million, or 9 cents per share, less than half of what Wall Street analysts had forecast. Revenue surged more than 90% from a year earlier. Elon Musk-led company said it was on track to achieve a $100 billion annual revenue run rate by December.

Article Title: Oil price today: Crude steadies below $80 as Hormuz blockade keeps investors on edge
Article Text:
After two sessions of registering a fall, oil prices inched higher on Wednesday, as the crucial Strait of Hormuz continues to see disruption.

Oil prices rose slightly on Wednesday after two days of steep losses, with markets closely watching efforts to end the US-Iran war and restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude futures rose 31 cents, or 0.39%, to $79.67 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 11 cents, or 0.15%, to $75.88 a barrel.The modest recovery comes after steep losses seen earlier in the week. Earlier on Tuesday, Qatar said that mediators were making progress in efforts to end the conflict. The comments pushed oil prices lower, although Tehran denied US President Donald Trump's claim that talks were already under way.Brent settled below $80 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since July 13.“The main sticking point appears to be whether Iran will continue to insist on a degree of control over the waterway, and whether the US will stand its ground and refuse that outcome,” analysts from IG said in a note cited by Reuters.Brent had closed more than 5% lower on Tuesday, extending the sharp declines recorded on Monday amid hopes that an agreement could be reached soon.Before the war began, around 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passed through the Strait of Hormuz. In March alone, oil prices had risen 50%.Qatar's Emiri office said US President Donald Trump and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani discussed efforts to narrow differences between Washington and Tehran and improve the prospects for a lasting settlement during a phone call on Tuesday.Trump said on Monday that talks with Tehran had begun and described the situation as Iran's "last chance" to reach a deal. Iranian officials, however, maintained that no negotiations with the United States were taking place.Market participants were also awaiting official US inventory data later on Wednesday.According to market sources citing figures from the American Petroleum Institute, US crude and gasoline inventories increased last week, while distillate stocks declined.Crude inventories rose by about 2.7 million barrels in the week ended July 31, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity.Official inventory data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), the statistical arm of the US Department of Energy, is scheduled to be released at 10:30 am ET (1430 GMT) on Wednesday.Meanwhile, even as global crude benchmarks have continued to inch higher, the spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel levels seen earlier during the conflict.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose 31 cents, or 0.39%, to $79.67 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 11 cents to $75.88 a barrel. The modest recovery comes after steep losses seen earlier in the week. Qatar said that mediators were making progress in efforts to end the conflict.

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street near new record high as earnings drive rally; crude prices slip
Article Text:
Such growth would be the strongest earnings expansion since the extraordinary rebound in the spring of 2021.

US stock market today: Wall Street moved closer to fresh record highs on Tuesday as easing oil prices and another round of strong corporate earnings lifted investor sentiment.The S&P 500 gained 0.6% and was on course to surpass its previous record closing high set earlier this summer. By 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had climbed 658 points, or 1.2%, extending gains beyond the record it set a day earlier, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.1%.Despite persistent concerns over elevated inflation, the Iran conflict and the possibility of an AI-driven stock market bubble, Wall Street has continued to scale new highs, supported by robust corporate earnings.According to an AP report, Palantir Technologies was among the top gainers, with its shares soaring 19.8% after Chief Executive Officer Alex Karp said the company's revenue had surged 93% year-on-year during the spring quarter, describing it as an "otherworldly" quarter. Along with reporting quarterly earnings that exceeded analysts' expectations, the AI software company also raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance.Caterpillar shares jumped 10.5% after the heavy equipment manufacturer posted quarterly profit and revenue that surpassed market estimates. The company also crossed the $20 billion mark in quarterly sales and revenue for the first time. CEO Joe Creed said Caterpillar continued to witness strong order inflows and an expanding backlog across its core businesses.The two companies added to a growing list of firms such as Amazon and Microsoft, that have delivered stronger-than-expected quarterly results.According to FactSet, companies in the S&P 500 were expected to report nearly 50% year-on-year growth in earnings per share for the spring quarter heading into this week.Such growth would be the strongest earnings expansion since the extraordinary rebound in the spring of 2021, when the US economy was recovering rapidly from the COVID-19 pandemic.Equities also received support from another decline in crude oil prices on Tuesday.Brent crude, the global benchmark, fell 4.2% to $80.29 a barrel as optimism once again replaced fear in the oil market. Throughout July, prices fluctuated sharply between $72 and $102 a barrel amid uncertainty over when the conflict with Iran would allow oil tankers to resume unrestricted movement through the Persian Gulf. As geopolitical developments shifted, crude prices repeatedly swung between gains and losses.The latest decline in oil prices also pushed bond yields lower, easing pressure on both the broader economy and financial markets.The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note dropped to 4.63%, compared with 4.70% on Monday and 4.75% at the end of last week. Although this marked a significant move in the bond market, yields remained considerably higher than the 3.97% level seen before the Iran conflict began.Across international markets, equity indices posted modest gains in most parts of Europe and Asia.South Korea stood out, with the Kospi advancing 1.6%. The benchmark has witnessed some of the sharpest swings globally in recent weeks because it is heavily weighted towards AI-linked technology giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.The Kospi had fallen 5.1% before rebounding 17.9% over the previous two trading sessions.Semiconductor stocks also traded higher on Wall Street, providing strong support to the broader market. Nvidia rose 2.4%, Micron Technology climbed 6.9%, and Broadcom gained 4.7%, making them among the biggest contributors to the S&P 500's advance.
Article Summary: The S&P 500 gained 0.6% and was on course to surpass its previous record closing high set earlier this summer. By 9:35 a.m. Eastern time, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had climbed 658 points, or 1.2%, extending gains beyond the record it set a day earlier. Palantir Technologies was among the top gainers, with its shares soaring 19.8% after reporting quarterly earnings that exceeded analysts' expectations.

Article Title: Friendship with benefits: Why Trump is helping Japan rescue the yen
Article Text:
Why a weaker dollar suits US president Trump (Photo credit: Reuters)

Catch up quick



US has taken the extraordinary step of helping after Japan interest rates remain well below peers.



Why it matters: Japan’s Treasury threat



Between the lines: A weaker dollar suits Trump



A weak yen makes Japanese products cheaper in dollar terms.

The big picture: Containing an Asian chain reaction



Reality check: Intervention buys time, not strength



The US has taken the extraordinary step of helping Japan pull the yen back from a four-decade low, signalling that Washington sees the currency’s collapse as more than Tokyo’s economic problem.The joint intervention drove the yen from nearly 164 against the dollar last month to around 155.20 on Monday before it settled near 157. Japan may have spent as much as $36.58 billion buying yen during Friday’s operation, according to central bank data cited by Reuters. The US Treasury reportedly sold euros, not dollars, to purchase yen.This was the first coordinated US-Japan currency intervention since the aftermath of Japan’s devastating earthquake and tsunami in 2011. More importantly, it was the first joint attempt in almost three decades to strengthen, rather than weaken, the yen.The operation may have been presented as assistance to a trusted ally. But Washington is also protecting US Treasury markets, American exporters and the wider Asian financial system.The dollar had climbed above 163 yen, its strongest level against the Japanese currency in about 40 years, before suspicions of official intervention pushed it below 160 late last week.After both governments acknowledged the operation, the dollar briefly fell to nearly 155.20 yen. In currency markets, where daily movements are generally measured in fractions, that was a dramatic correction.Japanese finance minister Satsuki Katayama confirmed that Tokyo had bought yen in coordination with the US Treasury Department."We will not hesitate to conduct further joint intervention," she said.President Donald Trump described the decision as help for an important ally. "We have a good relationship with Japan. We’re very strong — very, very strong financially and they are, you know, they have a weakening yen, and they wanted a little bit of help, and we’re always there for Japan. Japan’s been very good to us, with the exception, of course, of Pearl Harbor."Trump said the US received a "financial benefit" from the operation and called it a "signal of friendship." "It’s also good for the world economy," he added.The public acknowledgment itself was unusual. Currency interventions are often kept deliberately opaque so that traders remain uncertain about it.The most immediate US concern is not the exchange rate alone. It is what Japan might need to sell to defend it.Japan is the largest foreign holder of US government debt, owning more than $1.1 trillion in Treasuries. Its overall portfolio of US Treasuries, equities and other assets is close to $3 trillion, according to the New York Times. That includes nearly $1.2 trillion in American equities and more than $300 billion in corporate debt.To buy yen, Tokyo ordinarily obtains dollars from its foreign-exchange reserves, which include huge holdings of US government bonds. If repeated intervention forced Japan to unload Treasuries on a large scale, bond prices could fall and yields could rise.That would translate into higher borrowing costs for the US government at a time when long-term Treasury yields are already under pressure from inflation concerns. The New York Times noted that the 30-year Treasury yield recently reached its highest level since 2007."For Washington, supporting the yen is relatively low-cost insurance," Moody’s Analytics economist John Bromhead wrote in a note cited by the New York Times.Washington is therefore helping Japan avoid—or at least limit—a potentially destabilising liquidation of US debt. The Federal Reserve’s standing repo facility for foreign monetary authorities provides another line of defence: Japan can temporarily exchange Treasury securities for dollars instead of selling those bonds outright. The Fed says the facility was designed partly to prevent foreign demand for dollar liquidity from disrupting US financial markets.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has indicated that Washington could consider expanding access to that backstop in the coming months.The intervention also fits Trump’s longstanding concern that an excessively strong dollar puts American companies at a disadvantage.A weak yen makes Japanese products cheaper in dollar terms, helping Japan’s manufacturers compete in the US. At the same time, American machinery, agricultural products and other exports become more expensive for Japanese buyers.The imbalance is substantial. The US imported about $146 billion in goods from Japan last year while exporting roughly $82 billion, according to US trade data cited by the New York Times.A stronger yen makes US products more competitive in Japan. It also reduces some of the price advantage enjoyed by Japanese exporters, particularly in sectors such as automobiles and industrial equipment."It’s very rare that the Americans will work with the Japanese on this, but there is an alignment of interests here basically between Japan and America," Astris Advisory Japan strategist Neil Newman told the Associated Press.The Financial Times framed the move as the emergence of a more interventionist US currency policy under Bessent. His willingness to attack a market trade that conflicts with Washington’s interests has forced investors to consider whether the Treasury might act elsewhere."The US Treasury’s arrival marks a new sheriff in town, warning speculators away from selling the yen," ING’s global head of markets Chris Turner told the FT, saying it "marks a return to an age of FX activism" .The yen is not a peripheral currency. It is the world’s third most traded currency after the dollar and euro, according to Bank for International Settlements data cited by the New York Times.Its sharp depreciation can drag down currencies such as the South Korean won as investors reassess the competitiveness of Asian exporters. Governments across the region may then have to spend dollar reserves to support their currencies.That creates two dangers for Washington. Asian central banks might sell US Treasuries to raise dollars, pushing American yields higher. Competitive currency depreciation could also make Asian exports cheaper in the US, blunting the impact of Trump’s tariffs.The US intervention is consequently aimed at preventing a Japanese currency crisis from turning into a regional rush for dollars and a broader sell-off in US bonds.There is a geopolitical dimension as well. Japan is a central US ally in Asia and an important part of Washington’s strategic architecture for balancing China. A currency-driven cost-of-living crisis could weaken Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government and complicate economic and security cooperation.Oxford Economics’ Shigeto Nagai called the move a "low-cost" favour to an ally that simultaneously protects currency and bond-market stability.The joint action has made betting against the yen riskier. US participation adds far more credibility than another unilateral Japanese intervention, particularly after Tokyo’s previous efforts produced only temporary rallies.But neither government has removed the fundamental causes of yen weakness.The Bank of Japan’s benchmark rate is 1%, its highest in 31 years but still far below the Federal Reserve’s 3.5%-3.75% range. That gap encourages investors to borrow cheaply in yen and move money into higher-yielding dollar assets.Japan also imports most of its energy. Higher oil prices caused by the Iran war increase the country’s dollar bill, intensifying demand for foreign currency and worsening domestic inflation.At the same time, Takaichi is advocating heavier government spending and a reduction in the sales tax on food from 8% to 1%. Those policies could add to inflation and deepen concerns about a national debt already exceeding twice the size of Japan’s economy."If Japan wants a higher yen, it needs to address the monetary and fiscal policy concerns," former US Treasury official Mark Sobel told Reuters.The Bank of Japan is now under pressure to reinforce the intervention with another interest-rate increase, possibly as early as September. Yet raising rates too quickly could hurt growth, shake Japan’s bond market and make domestic assets more attractive than US securities, creating another potential headache for Washington."The yield differential remains wide, Japan’s energy-import burden remains significant, and the Bank of Japan is still moving more slowly than the market would normally require to generate a sustained currency reversal," SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes said in commentary cited by the Associated Press.The joint operation has changed the calculation for traders, but not the economic equation. Washington is helping Japan rescue the yen because the alternative: a weaker Asian currency, Treasury sell-offs, higher US borrowing costs and a stronger dollar, could prove far more costly for the United States.
Article Summary: US has taken the extraordinary step of helping after Japan interest rates remain well below peers. Japan may have spent as much as $36.58 billion buying yen during Friday’s operation, according to central bank data. The US Treasury reportedly sold euros, not dollars, to purchase yen.

Article Title: Oil rebounds from three-week low as Hormuz tensions keep supply fears alive
Article Text: Oil prices rebounded modestly on Tuesday after posting their biggest single-day decline in weeks in the previous session.Benchmark oil prices extended their recovery, with Brent crude climbing $0.49, or 0.58%, to $84.26 a barrel, while WTI crude advanced $0.41, or 0.51%, to $80.75 a barrel around 7:20 am IST.The rebound followed Monday's 7% slide, which had pushed the benchmark to its lowest level in three weeks. Markets had sold off after US President Donald Trump said that he was pausing any fresh military action against Iran while efforts continued to end the conflict and resolve competing claims over the Strait of Hormuz.The waterway, a vital route for Gulf oil exports, handled energy shipments equivalent to around one-fifth of global consumption each day before the conflict began disrupting trade. Even so, prospects of a negotiated outcome remained uncertain after Iran dismissed Trump's remarks.Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said that no talks with Washington were under way and that no meetings had been arranged, contradicting Trump's assertion that negotiations were in progress.The future of the Strait of Hormuz also remains a key point of contention. The United States maintains that a memorandum of understanding agreed in June committed Iran to reopening the passage, while Tehran argues the text explicitly safeguarded its authority over the strait.Signs of changing shipping patterns have continued to emerge. Barclays analysts said that crude and refined product exports through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 4.2 million barrels a day in the week ended July 31, compared with 3.2 million barrels a day the week before, Reuters reported.Shipping data also showed six Saudi-flagged supertankers recently altered their route in the Gulf of Aden and are now sailing towards southern Africa. At the same time, two vessels carrying Saudi crude crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Oman has also slowed following reports of attacks on vessels.Fresh concerns surfaced on Tuesday after the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations received a report from a cargo vessel that said it had been struck by an unknown projectile about 20 nautical miles (37 km) northeast of Oman's Al Khasab.Market participants said the latest developments suggest that risks to energy supplies remain despite the pause in military action."Some of the sting has been taken out of oil prices ... with Trump pausing strikes on Iran and touting a return to negotiations (though) the move lower remains fragile -- oil could just as easily rebound higher if missiles start flying again or if tankers around the Strait of Hormuz come under fire once more," Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade told Reuters.Even though oil prices have continued to climb, they remain below the earlier peak of $126 per barrel reached during the previous surge.
Article Summary: Brent crude climbs 0.58% to $84.26 a barrel, while WTI crude advances 0.51%. The rebound followed Monday's 7% slide, which had pushed the benchmark to its lowest level in three weeks. Markets sold off after US President Donald Trump said that he was pausing any fresh military action against Iran.

Article Title: Amazon achieves new milestone! Market cap crosses $3 trillion as AI, cloud growth power stock rally
Article Text:
Amazon and Microsoft are the only two whose heavy AI investments have been rewarded by investors. (AP photo)

Yet another technology stock has crossed the $3 trillion market cap. Amazon's market capitalisation went past the $3 trillion mark for the first time on Monday, driven by a sharp rally after the company reported strong quarterly results and reinforced investor confidence that the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is generating fresh demand for its cloud-computing business, its biggest profit driver.The stock was last trading 5.5% higher at $286.20, a record high, taking its gains for the year to more than 23%.Shares of the Seattle-headquartered e-commerce and cloud giant had surged 15% on Friday after the company reported its fastest cloud revenue growth in over four years and increased its forecast for annual capital expenditure.Among the "Magnificent Seven" technology companies that have reported earnings so far, Amazon and Microsoft are the only two whose heavy AI investments have been rewarded by investors. In contrast, Tesla, Alphabet and Meta came under pressure as their aggressive spending plans weighed on free cash flow during the latest quarter.Like several other technology giants, Amazon has been investing billions of dollars to expand its AI infrastructure. In April, the company announced a fresh investment in Anthropic, following its earlier commitment this year to invest up to $50 billion in OpenAI.Founded by Jeff Bezos in 1994, Amazon took just over two years to add another $1 trillion to its market value after first crossing the $2 trillion milestone in June 2024.Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet and Nvidia are the other companies that have previously achieved a market capitalisation of at least $3 trillion.Nvidia currently holds the title of the world's most valuable company, with a market capitalisation approaching $5 trillion.The artificial intelligence AI boom has propelled global stock markets to record levels, with leading technology companies committing hundreds of billions of dollars to expand AI infrastructure and capabilities. The strong AI-led rally has also helped equities withstand the risks and uncertainty arising from the Iran conflict, supporting broader market sentiment despite geopolitical tensions.However, recently technology stocks globally have come under pressure raising doubts about the sustainability of the rally and concerns of a bubble.
Article Summary: The stock was last trading 5.5% higher at $286.20, a record high. The Seattle- headquartered e-commerce and cloud giant had surged 15% on Friday after the company reported its fastest cloud revenue growth in over four years. Amazon has been investing billions of dollars to expand its AI infrastructure.

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street rallies over 1% on falling oil prices, hopes of deal with Iran
Article Text:
Oil prices declined on Monday, providing relief to Wall Street by easing concerns that inflationary pressures could intensify further.

US stock market today:The S&P 500 gained 1%, extending its recovery after a turbulent July marked by sharp swings. The Dow Jones Industrial Average had advanced 624 points, or 1.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite was up over 1% as oil prices dropped and hopes of a US-Iran deal lifted market sentiment.Oil prices declined on Monday, providing relief to Wall Street by easing concerns that inflationary pressures could intensify further. The softer crude prices lifted US equities, although financial markets continued to witness significant volatility, according to an AP report.The biggest move came from the oil market, where Brent crude fell 4.9% to $83.65 per barrel. Prices retreated after President Donald Trump said over the weekend that he had decided against authorising fresh US military strikes on Iran following appeals from regional allies.Last month, Brent crude fluctuated sharply between $72 and $102 a barrel as sentiment shifted repeatedly over the prospects of oil tankers resuming unrestricted movement through the Persian Gulf following the Iran conflict.Trump's latest decision on Iran helped ease fears of a renewed surge in inflation. As a result, Treasury yields also moved lower, reflecting reduced inflation expectations in the bond market.The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note declined to 4.68% from 4.75% at Friday's close. Even so, it remained well above the 3.97% level seen before the outbreak of the Iran conflict.The sharp rise in bond yields since then has raised concerns for financial markets, as higher borrowing costs can weigh on stock valuations and slow economic activity by making loans more expensive for households and businesses.
